players.product: Turnkey HPC data-center campuses leased to hyperscalers (Barber Lake, Black Pearl, Stingray - Texas) - ex-Bitcoin-mining, now 'Cipher Digital'

quarterly_data.quarter: Cipher Digital press release: Cipher Digital Expands Barber Lake Lease Term to 20 Years, (09-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Cipher Digital extended the contracted lease duration of its Barber Lake data center (Colorado City, Texas) from 10 years to 20 years, raising total contracted revenue at the facility from $3.8 billion to over $9 billion: an amendment to the existing Barber Lake Lease with Fluidstack is coupled with a binding commitment from an unnamed 'leading AI lab' to lease the facility for an additional 10-year term after the Fluidstack lease ends, under a separate lease with substantially consistent economics, expected to generate approximately $5.2 billion of incremental contracted revenue. CEO Tyler Page: the transaction underscores 'the durability of demand for hyperscale computing capacity'.
quarterly_data.figure: 10 to 20 years; contracted revenue $3.8 billion to over $9 billion; ~$5.2 billion incremental

quarterly_data.quarter: Cipher Digital press release: Cipher Digital Expands Barber Lake Lease Term to 20 Years, (09-25-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Barber Lake delivery schedule revised: in connection with change orders and evolving tenant requirements, the lease amendment sets phased delivery with individual data halls expected from the fourth quarter of 2026 through the first quarter of 2027; rent commences per data hall on delivery, with the first rent commencement expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, and Cipher says it is on track with the revised schedule. Under a cost reimbursement framework with Fluidstack and the AI lab, Cipher bears the first $359.3 million of costs above the initial budget, and the tenant reimburses 50% of costs above that amount over the twenty-year term as additional rent at a contracted rate of return.
quarterly_data.figure: data halls Q4 2026 through Q1 2027; first rent Q4 2026; first $359.3 million of overruns borne by Cipher; 50% above that reimbursed
